clue.text: One that doesn't forget carrying one in this

definitions.text: One that doesn't forget carrying one in this

parts.words: One that doesn't forget carrying one in this
parts.note: the creature that never forgets is the elephant, and this is the canopied seat it carries a rider in

explanation.walkthrough: 'An elephant never forgets' is the proverb behind 'One that doesn't forget'; the second 'one' is the rider sitting on its back.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description of the seat with a canopy strapped onto an elephant's back for riders.

clue.text: Husband a little impolite, heading off for convention

parts.note: a bit means a little

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the word for impolite is removed

parts.note: rude means impolite

explanation.surface: A husband is mildly rude and gets sent off to a conference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convention' looks like a gathering but means custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Habitude means customary practice or habit, a synonym for convention in its sense of custom.

clue.text: In which partners are split without love

definitions.text: In which partners are split without love

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the partners are placed around the love

parts.note: in bridge, West and East are partners, abbreviated W and E
love is zero in tennis scores, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A couple separate because love has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: W and E (bridge partners) are split by O (love, nil). The whole clue also describes misery when a couple parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Woe is deep sorrow, the state lovers fall into when they separate without love.

clue.text: Holy book's line accepted by a man from Asia, not European

indicators.note: accepted by says the line is taken inside the following words

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: not means the European is left out of the Asian man

parts.note: a Korean is a man from Korea in Asia

explanation.surface: A man from Asia, not a European, accepts a line from a scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: A KORAN (KOREAN less E) takes in L.
explanation.definitionFit: Alkoran is an archaic name for the Koran, the holy book of Islam.

clue.text: Like DD girl's pair up front!

indicators.note: up front says the word for a pair is placed ahead of the girl's name

parts.note: a pair is two
Penny is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A remark about a woman with a DD-cup bra, shown off up front.
explanation.walkthrough: DD reads as a bra size but is two old pennies: d was the abbreviation for a penny in pre-decimal British money.
explanation.definitionFit: D stood for the old British penny, so DD is a sum worth two pence, an adjective sense.

clue.text: Lad with lip by cracker, possibly with merest hint of smoked kipper?

parts.note: one who cracks a whip could be called a whipper

indicators.note: merest hint of means only the opening letter of smoked is taken

parts.note: kip is slang for sleep, so a kipper is one who naps, a napper

explanation.surface: A cheeky boy eats a cracker with a smoked kipper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kipper' is not the fish but someone having a kip (a nap).
explanation.definitionFit: A whippersnapper is a cheeky, presumptuous young person, a lad with lip.

clue.text: Bar in front of opening

parts.note: pre- means before or in front of
a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: A bar stands before an opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' is a verb, to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar something is to stop it happening, the same as to prevent it.

clue.text: Expanded new and old compound

parts.note: new gives N and old gives O, and NO, a chemical formula, is written out in full as its name

explanation.surface: A compound that is both new and old has been enlarged.
explanation.walkthrough: N (new) and O (old) make NO, the chemical formula of this gas; 'Expanded' asks for the formula spelt out as its full name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitric oxide is a chemical compound of nitrogen and oxygen, a colourless gas.

clue.text: Long ago, securing a thousand. runs — but none off this?

indicators.note: securing means the word for long ago holds the thousand inside

parts.note: yore means long ago, as in days of yore
K is the abbreviation for a thousand
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Long ago a batsman reached a thousand runs, but not off this ball.
explanation.walkthrough: A yorker is a cricket delivery pitched right at the batsman's feet, very hard to score runs off, hence 'none off this'.
explanation.definitionFit: A yorker is a ball pitched at the batsman's toes, from which scoring is hard, so few or no runs come.

clue.text: Direct current son gets in a few detached spots

parts.note: to direct a flow is to channel it
I is the symbol for electric current
a plane that gets in lands

explanation.surface: A son's journey on direct current gets him to a few remote places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direct current' looks like DC but is two pieces. The Channel Islands are British dependencies off the French coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Channel Islands are a small group of islands lying apart from the mainland, a few detached spots of land.

clue.text: Perhaps get techie to relieve tension

parts.note: breaking up the letters of the phrase 'the ice' would perhaps give the word techie

explanation.surface: A suggestion to fetch an IT person to calm a fraught office.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: break (rearrange) THE ICE and you get TECHIE. 'Perhaps' marks that this is one possible outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to ease awkwardness or strain when people first meet, so it serves as relieving tension.

clue.text: God! Taken by surprise by progressive letters

annotationWithheld.why: God! Taken by surprise by progressive letters (3): one indicator, 'progressive letters', takes the 1st letter of Taken, 2nd of by and 3rd of surprise (T, Y, R); the grammar needs an indicator per pick, so the parse cannot be written
annotationWithheld.clue: God! Taken by surprise by progressive letters

clue.text: City goddess put in a number of commandments

indicators.note: put in says the goddess's name goes inside the number

parts.note: there are ten commandments
Hera is the Greek queen of the gods

explanation.surface: A goddess is placed among the commandments given to Moses.
explanation.definitionFit: An older spelling of Tehran, the capital city of Iran.

clue.text: Operetta's. discordant harmonies, loud and'soft

indicators.note: discordant suggests harmonies jarring, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
F (forte) is the musical abbreviation for loud
P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: A light opera has jarring harmonies played both loud and soft.
explanation.walkthrough: HARMONIES with F and P is rearranged; the 's after Operetta is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Pinafore is a comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan, a well-known operetta.

clue.text: Chair legs regularly encircled by cats

indicators.note: encircled by says the letters from legs sit inside the word for cats

parts.note: a pride is a group of lions, big cats

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word legs, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Cats curl round the legs of a chair at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chair' is a verb here, not the furniture the surface suggests, and 'cats' are lions rather than pets.
explanation.definitionFit: To chair a meeting is to preside over it, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Breaking down is confusing what comes next …

indicators.note: confusing tells us to jumble the letters of the answer that follows

parts.note: what comes next points to the following entry, 17 across, whose letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that collapse is bewildering, trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 and 17 across are anagrams of each other: each clue rearranges the other's answer, and the two clues read as one sentence across the ellipsis.
explanation.definitionFit: Disintegration is the process of falling apart, so it means breaking down as a noun.

clue.text: Shaken 'old comedian held up

indicators.note: held says the old word holds the comedian inside it

parts.note: aged means old

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the comedian's name is written bottom to top

parts.note: Jacques Tati was a French film comedian

explanation.surface: An elderly comic was robbed at gunpoint and left rattled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' looks like a robbery but is two signals: ITAT (TATI going up) is held in AGED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be agitated is to be stirred up and upset, the same as being shaken.

clue.text: … what comes before breaking down is confusing

indicators.note: breaking down tells us to take apart and rebuild the letters of the previous answer

parts.note: what comes before points to the preceding entry, 15 across, whose letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The tail of a sentence saying a collapse bewilders.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue was only the ellipsis; the page prints the full words. This clue mirrors 15 across: its answer is the anagram of that one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disorientating leaves you bewildered and lost, hence confusing as an adjective.

clue.text: Excluded 'drunk

definitions.meaning: left out of things, not part of the group
so intoxicated as to be unaware of what is going on

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both left out of the action and too intoxicated to function.

clue.text: Late opening that's official?

parts.note: the late here are the dead, so this is the formal cutting open of a body

explanation.walkthrough: 'Late opening' suggests shop hours, but 'the late' means the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: An autopsy is the formal post-mortem examination of a dead body, an official opening of the late.

clue.text: Gentleman changed in ultimate twist

indicators.note: changed in ultimate means the last letter of the gentleman's title is altered

parts.note: a squire is a country gentleman

explanation.surface: A gentleman is transformed by a final turn of fate.
explanation.walkthrough: SQUIRE has its last letter changed; the clue does not say what to, so the crossing letters must supply the M.
explanation.definitionFit: To squirm is to wriggle and writhe, to twist the body about.

clue.text: Moving step by step, I left bird eating insect

indicators.note: eating says the bird swallows the insect, holding it inside
left means the letter I has departed from the bird's name

parts.note: the quail is a small game bird
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bird that has lost its I hops forward, snacking on a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: Quantal describes change in discrete jumps, like quantum steps, rather than a smooth flow.

clue.text: One's dropped into open case

indicators.note: dropped into says the letter for one goes inside the word for open

parts.note: patent means open, plain to see
one is I, the Roman numeral, and 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A single item falls into an unlocked suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' is a medical case, not luggage; 'open' is PATENT in its sense of obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor speaks of a person under treatment as a case, so patient fits.

clue.text: Tribesman put sash round

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the word for sash is read backwards

parts.note: an obi is a broad Japanese sash worn with a kimono

explanation.surface: A tribesman ties a sash about himself.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ibo (Igbo) are a people of south-eastern Nigeria, so one member is a tribesman.

clue.text: Digital ID code

parts.note: digital here means made by a finger, so this is a mark that identifies someone

explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' suggests computers, but here means of the digits, the fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description of the unique pattern of ridges on a fingertip, used to identify people.

clue.text: Prepared tongue in humidor.

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the word humidor

explanation.surface: Cured ox tongue is kept in a cigar box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepared tongue' sounds like the deli meat, but means a constructed language.
explanation.definitionFit: Ido is an artificial language devised as a reformed Esperanto, so a made-up tongue.

clue.text: Surprisingly, so-so team scored : majestically.

indicators.note: surprisingly says the letters of so-so team end up in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An average side unexpectedly plays with grandeur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scored' looks like a sporting result but points to a musical score, where the answer is a tempo marking.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestoso is the Italian musical direction to play in a stately, dignified manner.

clue.text: Catholic goes across unknown little path

indicators.note: goes across says the word for catholic spans the unknown, holding it inside

parts.note: catholic with a small c means broad, wide-ranging
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A Catholic crosses a minor footpath.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C is a disguise: 'catholic' in its general sense means broad or universal.
explanation.definitionFit: A byroad is a minor side road, so it fits a small path or way.
